problem:
The following table shows the number of customers per minute, $c(t),$ that arrive at a shop counter over a period of $120$ minutes.

| $t\,(\text{minutes})$ | $0$ | $30$ | $80$ | $120$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $c(t)\,(\text{customers/minute})$ | $10$ | $8$ | $6$ | $12$ |

Use the trapezoidal rule with the partition

$$
[0,30]\cup [30,80]\cup [80,120],
$$

to approximate the total number of customers served in two hours.

activity_context.topic_title: Approximating Areas With the Trapezoidal Rule

feedback.problem:
Using the trapezoidal rule with the partition

$$
[-1,2]=[-1,0]\cup [0,2],
$$

approximate the area under the curve of the function $y=\frac{10}{1+{x}^{2}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{10}{1+{x}^{2}}.$ Let's plot this function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14067661/assets/c4c9aa8e615747199462e0597f4cb7be82031efdb5b2f6585e3fb9c0b652ee78.png)

We've drawn some trapezoids to help calculate our trapezoidal rule sum. By calculating the area of each trapezoid, we obtain the following approximation for our area $A:$

$$
A≈\overset{1\text{st trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(-1)+f(0)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{1}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}+\overset{2\text{nd trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(0)+f(2)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{2}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}
$$

Substituting the appropriate numbers into the above expression gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈\frac{5+10}{2}\cdot (0-(-1))+\frac{10+2}{2}\cdot (2-0) \\  & =\frac{15}{2}\cdot 1+\frac{12}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{15}{2}+12 \\  & =\frac{39}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
